title: 21-Day Response Window
description: An infraction defendant must appear or post bail within 21 days of the notice to appear; otherwise a civil assessment and collections referral may follow.
ai_version: In LA County you have 21 days from your ticket date to pay or ask for a hearing. Miss it and the court can decide against you and add a collection fee.
name: ca-vc-§40519

title: Traffic School Masks One Point
description: An eligible driver may attend traffic school once per 18 months to mask one point from a qualifying moving violation.
ai_version: In LA County you can take traffic school once every 18 months to hide one point from your record.
name: ca-la-ts-1

title: 11-Point Suspension Threshold
description: Accumulating 11 points within 18 months may result in license suspension; a warning is appropriate well before that.
ai_version: In NYC, 11 points in 18 months can get your license suspended — we flag a warning at 6.
name: ny-vtl-§510

title: No Calibration Records → Dismissal
description: If the agency cannot produce radar/lidar calibration records on timely request, the speed reading is unreliable and the citation must be dismissed.
ai_version: In Travis County, if the police can't show their radar was calibrated, a speeding ticket can be thrown out — exactly what happened on TC-2026-0003.
name: tx-aus-ab-2025-114

title: 14-Day Response Window
description: A defendant must respond to a citation within the period stated on the notice, commonly 14 days, or a warrant and additional fees may issue.
ai_version: In Travis County you usually have 14 days to respond to a ticket before a warrant and extra fees can be added.
name: tx-tc-§543
